title: Ask My Aunt's Ledger  (Le registre de ma tante)

segments.t: À la réception, tandis que tombe le soir du samedi, Hannah et Mademoiselle Evelyn posent la partition manuscrite sous la lampe du comptoir devant Arthur. Écoutez d'abord toute la scène.
Arthur, look what was hiding inside the upright piano in Room Nine!
Handwritten music? Let me pull my glasses down... wait a second!
Do you know who wrote 'Courtyard Waltz' thirty years ago, Arthur?
Look at those round capital letters. That is my aunt's handwriting!
Your aunt played the piano and ran the Friday tea room?!
She baked cakes in the morning and wrote little songs at night!
Why did she stop halfway through page two in May thirty years ago?
Her old green guest book from that spring is still in the attic chest!
Wait, the front desk telephone is blinking with a recorded voice message.
Press play, Hannah! Who calls on Saturday evening?!
It is the city heritage office... they moved our cafe inspection to Wednesday at three!
Wednesday at three?! That gives us three days instead of six!
Parcourons ligne par ligne cette révélation de fin d'épisode.
Arthur, look what was hiding inside the upright piano in Room Nine!
'Arthur, regardez ce qui se cachait dans le piano droit de la chambre neuf!'
Handwritten music? Let me pull my glasses down... wait a second!
'De la musique écrite à la main? Laissez-moi abaisser mes lunettes... attendez une seconde!'
Do you know who wrote 'Courtyard Waltz' thirty years ago, Arthur?
'Savez-vous qui a composé la "Valse de la Cour" il y a trente ans, Arthur?'
Look at those round capital letters. That is my aunt's handwriting!
'Regardez ces majuscules bien rondes. C'est l'écriture de ma tante!'
Your aunt played the piano and ran the Friday tea room?!
'Votre tante jouait du piano et tenait le salon de thé du vendredi?!'
She baked cakes in the morning and wrote little songs at night!
'Elle faisait cuire des gâteaux le matin et composait de petits airs la nuit!'
Why did she stop halfway through page two in May thirty years ago?
'Pourquoi s'est-elle arrêtée à mi-chemin de la page deux en mai il y a trente ans?'
Her old green guest book from that spring is still in the attic chest!
'Son vieux livre d'or vert de ce printemps-là est encore dans le coffre du grenier!'
Wait, the front desk telephone is blinking with a recorded voice message.
'Attendez, le téléphone de la réception clignote avec un message vocal enregistré.'
Press play, Hannah! Who calls on Saturday evening?!
'Appuyez sur lecture, Hannah! Qui appelle un samedi soir?!'
It is the city heritage office... they moved our cafe inspection to Wednesday at three!
'C'est le service municipal du patrimoine... ils ont avancé l'inspection de notre café à mercredi, trois heures!'
Wednesday at three?! That gives us three days instead of six!
'Mercredi à trois heures?! Cela nous laisse trois jours au lieu de six!'
Réécoutons toute cette scène finale.

Your aunt played the piano and ran the Friday tea room?!
She baked cakes in the morning and wrote little songs at night!
Why did she stop halfway through page two in May thirty years ago?
Her old green guest book from that spring is still in the attic chest!
Wait, the front desk telephone is blinking with a recorded voice message.
Press play, Hannah! Who calls on Saturday evening?!
It is the city heritage office... they moved our cafe inspection to Wednesday at three!
Wednesday at three?! That gives us three days instead of six!

La valse inachevée était de la main de la tante d'Arthur, et la visite du patrimoine vient d'être avancée de vendredi à mercredi trois heures! Bravo: le deuxième épisode est terminé. À très vite dans l'épisode trois!
Until tomorrow!
